Mathlib has docs#Partitions, an abstract structure on lattices, a predicate docs#Setoid.IsPartition on sets of sets and a type docs#Setoid.Partitions which bundles this predicate. I want to talk about preimages of partitions of sets by a function and the lattice structure on partitions of sets, and I would really like to do so in a way that has nice defeqs, in the sense that the members of the preimage are the preimages, and the members of the refinement are the intersections.

docs#Setoid.IsPartition is currently the only one being used for talking about partitions of sets, but it does so using setoids and prepositions which make it really a pain to define those structures in a way to have nice defeqs. The docs#Partition.completeLattice instance goes through choice and does not have any description of its elements. So isn't it the case that we should be developing docs#Partitions more and also be using it to talk about partitions of sets, especially to get nice descriptions of their algebraic operations?

The more far-fetched use case for me would be to talk about partitions in ergodic theory, but I was writing something else about measure theory and I noticed that I would like to have the partition [n, n + 1) of R\mathbb{R}R defined in Mathlib and be able to take preimages of it. But those are currently not straightforward things to do!

I want to talk about preimages of partitions of sets by a function and the lattice structure on partitions of sets, and I would really like to do so in a way that has nice defeqs, in the sense that the members of the preimage are the preimages, and the members of the refinement are the intersections.

What I did in my project is to use Setoids instead of partitions as we have a lot of APIs for it. e.g. pull back of a Setoid Setoid.comap, infimum of setoids Setoid.instInfSet, and also a lattice structure on the collection of Setoids Setoid.completeLattice

Note that we also have IndexedPartition that may be useful for your measure theory application (at least I used it here: IndexedPartition.aestronglyMeasurable_piecewise )
I think another good thing about the lattice version is that it can be used to define partitions of measurable sets with almost-sure equality (the quotient by the ideal of null measurable sets)
